_comment: Machine-readable reference list. Every id used in events/endings/facts/glossary/windows must exist here. 'kind': data = drives a mechanic · fact = verified statement · asset = 3D/texture/font/library · partner = space-agency partner. shared/references.md is generated from this file by shared/scripts/build-references.mjs. Portions generated with the assistance of an SI tool (Claude) and reviewed by Team PlutonyX.

sources.title: DONKI - Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information
sources.use: Solar flares, CMEs, particle events, Earth geomagnetic storms and WSA-ENLIL predicted arrivals at Mars. Drives the space-weather timeline of every mission, live or archived.
sources.note: Research-quality data; NOAA SWPC is the official forecast source. Also reachable through api.nasa.gov/DONKI.

sources.title: RadLab radiation dosimetry portal - instrument MSL-RAD-Surface (Curiosity rover Radiation Assessment Detector, Mars surface)
sources.use: Absorbed dose rate (µGy/h) measured on the surface of Mars. Sets the radiation dose of every sol and the minute-by-minute storm curve.

sources.title: Approximate Positions of the Planets (Keplerian elements, 1800-2050)
sources.use: Earth and Mars positions for the mission date: real distance and one-way radio delay; the mini solar-system map.

sources.title: Horizons System API
sources.use: Used only to check our radio-delay maths (agreement within 0.01 minute on three dates).

sources.org: USGS Astrogeology Science Center for NASA Mars 2020 · NASA/JPL/MSSS
sources.title: Mars 2020 Terrain Relative Navigation CTX DTM Mosaic (Jezero Crater, 20 m/pixel)
sources.use: Real elevation of Jezero Crater from Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Context Camera stereo images. The game terrain.

sources.org: USGS Astrogeology Science Center for NASA Mars 2020 · NASA/JPL/MSSS
sources.title: Mars 2020 Terrain Relative Navigation CTX Orthorectified Image Mosaic (Jezero Crater, 6 m/pixel)
sources.use: Real orbital image of Jezero Crater. The ground texture (greyscale image, tinted with Mars colours by us).

sources.title: Mars Trek
sources.use: Used to find and check the Jezero site, landing location and map layers.

sources.title: OSD-268: Microbiological and nutritional analysis of lettuce crops grown on the International Space Station - VEG-01B
sources.use: Evidence that lettuce grown in space was analysed as food. Basis for the greenhouse crops.

sources.title: OSD-269: Microbiological and nutritional analysis of lettuce crops grown on the International Space Station - VEG-03A
sources.use: Second Veggie lettuce harvest study.

sources.title: OSD-766: The microbial communities of a tomato crop grown in Veggie under different lighting regimes on the International Space Station
sources.use: Tomatoes and light 'recipes' in the greenhouse.

sources.title: Toolkit for educators and youth - Food production on the Moon and in remote areas
sources.use: Framing for the greenhouse and the classroom guide: food production in space, astronaut nutrition, benefits on Earth.

sources.org: European Space Agency (Solar Orbiter is an ESA/NASA mission)
sources.title: Can't stop won't stop: Solar Orbiter shows the Sun raging on
sources.use: Sunspot region AR3664 stayed active on the far side of the Sun; on 20 May 2024 Solar Orbiter's STIX saw a flare with an estimated class of X12.

sources.title: NASA Watches Mars Light Up During Epic Solar Storm (10 June 2024)
sources.use: 20 May 2024: X12 flare estimate; 8,100 micrograys = about 30 chest X-rays; biggest surge RAD has measured; cliffsides or lava tubes give extra shielding; camera 'snow'; MAVEN auroras.

sources.title: Large Solar Storm Sparks Global Aurora and Doubles Radiation Levels on the Martian Surface (29 Sept 2017)
sources.use: 11 Sept 2017 event: radiation more than double any earlier RAD reading for more than two days; aurora 25 times brighter; 'you would definitely want to take shelter'.

sources.title: NASA Says Mars Rover Discovered Potential Biosignature Last Year (10 Sept 2025)
sources.use: Cheyava Falls rock, Sapphire Canyon core, Bright Angel formation in Neretva Vallis, leopard spots, vivianite and greigite, 'potential biosignature', non-biological explanations not ruled out.

sources.title: Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit - Landing Site
sources.use: Jezero Crater: 28 miles (45 km) wide, lake about 3.5 billion years ago, river delta, Isidis Planitia.

sources.title: Mars: Facts
sources.use: Day length 24.6 hours; year 687 Earth days; sunlight takes 13 minutes; thin CO2 atmosphere; temperatures 20 C to about -153 C; no global magnetic field today; moons Phobos and Deimos; dust storms.

sources.title: NASA's Oxygen-Generating Experiment MOXIE Completes Mars Mission (6 Sept 2023)
sources.use: MOXIE made 122 g of oxygen from Mars air in 16 runs, up to 12 g per hour, 98 % pure or better.

sources.title: NASA Achieves Water Recovery Milestone on International Space Station (20 June 2023)
sources.use: 98 % water recovery; about a gallon per crew member per day.

sources.title: ICES-2017-87, 47th International Conference on Environmental Systems (oxygen requirement 0.84 kg per crew member per day)
sources.use: Oxygen need per person per day.

sources.title: Growing Plants in Space
sources.use: Veggie garden on the ISS: lettuce, mizuna, kale, zinnias; LEDs glow magenta pink; vitamins in packed food break down; plants help well-being.

sources.title: Opportunity Hunkers Down During Dust Storm (June 2018)
sources.use: 2018 dust storm: tau 10.8 (2007 storm: above 5.5); a quarter of the planet; rover could not charge; low-power fault mode.

sources.title: What Do Sunrises and Sunsets Look Like on Mars?
sources.use: Blue Martian sunset: fine dust scatters blue light forward.

sources.title: Speaking Percy's Language: How to Talk so Perseverance Will Listen
sources.use: Radio delay between Earth and Mars: roughly 3 to 22 minutes depending on the planets' positions.

sources.title: Communication Delays, Disruptions, and Blackouts for Crewed Mars Missions (ASCEND 2022)
sources.use: NASA analysis of how delay forces crew independence.

sources.title: The Mars Relay Network Connects Us to NASA's Martian Explorers
sources.use: Surface missions send most data through orbiters.

sources.title: Mars Fact Sheet
sources.use: Mean surface gravity 3.73 m/s² (launch dust falls at this rate); sunlight at Mars 586.2 W/m² against 1361.0 at Earth (about 43 %).
